route_catalogue.name: Angers centre loop (Gare Saint-Laud, Ralliement, Jardin des Plantes, Château)
Drone survey, fields north of Angers

model.training_source: seeded synthetic normal runs on train routes only: Loire road, Maine road, Briollay loop, Belle-Beille loop, La Roseraie loop, two drone survey areas
model.risk_formula: risk = 100 * min(1, -log10(p) / 4), p = min(1, 2 * min(p_forest, p_tail))

limitations: All observations are deterministic synthetic output. One simulator produces every split, so these numbers are an upper bound on real-world performance.
Attack overlays are textbook versions: a careful adversary who matches C/N0 spread and clock behaviour would be harder to detect.
Route deviation assumes the vehicle follows an assigned route (delivery fleet, survey drone). A driver who changes route will look like drift.
One observation is one evaluation unit. A long attack contributes many correlated rows, so per-observation scores are not per-attack accuracy.
OSNMA status is simulated. A relay (meaconing) attack can pass OSNMA, which the stealth drift scenario shows.
